title: Confinement as Integrity Collapse: A Contract-Frozen Structural Signature of Quark Binding in the GCD/UMCP Measurement Kernel
object_of_study: The source-local integrity signature of the quark->hadron boundary under a frozen historical particle-data closure.
main_question: What structural signature does the quark->hadron boundary leave when quarks and hadrons are evaluated under a single frozen source-local particle-data closure?

claim_layers.claim: The source maps particles into bounded eight-channel trace vectors and computes the integrity composite IC = exp(κ); the kernel receives only the declared particle trace, not the QCD Lagrangian, a confining potential, Wilson loops, lattice configurations, or a running coupling.

Reported findings under the source-local closure: mean IC falls from 0.581 (quarks) to 0.0111 (hadrons), a 98.1% drop; all 14 conventional hadrons fall below the minimum quark IC of 0.517; the heterogeneity gap amplifies by 10.8x; the 14/14 bound holds across a guard-band sweep; six exotic hadrons fall in the hadron band.
Source-stated non-claims: not an analytic proof of QCD confinement, does not solve the Yang-Mills mass-gap problem, does not replace non-perturbative QCD.

The library places this as a historical hard-domain boundary case preserving the distinction between a structural signature computed under a declared historical adapter and a native QCD explanation; no current GCD closure or Tier-1 authority is implied.
